subject: ELA
title: ELA 3
description: A literature-rich third-grade English language arts course that integrates reading, writing, word study, grammar and speaking/listening every week. Students read fables, folktales, Greek myths, poetry, biographies and two classic novels (Charlotte's Web and The Wonderful Wizard of Oz), write narratives, informational reports, opinion essays and a short research report, and build decoding with prefixes, suffixes and multisyllable words.
framework: California Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy; 2014 CA ELA/ELD Framework

standards.RL.3.1: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text.
standards.RL.3.2: Recount stories, including fables, folktales and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details.
standards.RL.3.3: Describe characters (traits, motivations, feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.
standards.RL.3.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as used in a text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.
standards.RL.3.5: Refer to parts of stories, dramas and poems using terms such as chapter, scene and stanza; describe how each part builds on earlier sections.
standards.RL.3.6: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or characters.
standards.RL.3.7: Explain how illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story (mood, character, setting).
standards.RL.3.9: Compare and contrast themes, settings and plots of stories written by the same author about the same or similar characters.
standards.RL.3.10: Read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas and poetry, at the high end of the grades 2–3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
standards.RI.3.1: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of an informational text, referring explicitly to the text.
standards.RI.3.2: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.
standards.RI.3.3: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or steps in technical procedures using time, sequence and cause/effect language.
standards.RI.3.4: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a grade 3 text.
standards.RI.3.5: Use text features and search tools (key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information efficiently.
standards.RI.3.6: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.
standards.RI.3.7: Use information gained from illustrations (maps, photographs) and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding.
standards.RI.3.8: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence).
standards.RI.3.9: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.
standards.RI.3.10: Read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 2–3 band independently.
standards.RF.3.3a: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.
standards.RF.3.3b: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.
standards.RF.3.4a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
standards.RF.3.4b: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate and expression on successive readings.
standards.RF.3.4c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
standards.W.3.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons, linking words and a concluding statement.
standards.W.3.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas clearly, with facts, definitions, details, linking words and a conclusion.
standards.W.3.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences using descriptive details, dialogue, clear event sequences, temporal words and closure.
standards.W.3.4: With guidance and support, produce writing in which development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
standards.W.3.5: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing by planning, revising and editing.
standards.W.3.6: With guidance and support, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) and to interact and collaborate.
standards.W.3.7: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.
standards.W.3.8: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes and sort evidence into categories.
standards.W.3.10: Write routinely over extended and shorter time frames for a range of tasks, purposes and audiences.
standards.SL.3.1: Engage effectively in collaborative discussions, coming prepared, following agreed-upon rules, asking questions and explaining their own ideas.
standards.SL.3.2: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media.
standards.SL.3.3: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.
standards.SL.3.4: Report on a topic or text, tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.
standards.SL.3.5: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading; add visual displays when appropriate.
standards.SL.3.6: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.
standards.L.3.1a: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs in general and in particular sentences.
standards.L.3.1b: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.
standards.L.3.1d: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.
standards.L.3.1e: Form and use the simple (I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.
standards.L.3.1g: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, choosing between them.
standards.L.3.1i: Produce simple, compound and complex sentences.
standards.L.3.2c: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.
standards.L.3.2e: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words.
standards.L.3.2f: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts).
standards.L.3.2g: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, to check and correct spellings.
standards.L.3.3a: Choose words and phrases for effect.
standards.L.3.3b: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.
standards.L.3.4a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
standards.L.3.4b: Determine the meaning of a new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word.
standards.L.3.4c: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root.
standards.L.3.4d: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
standards.L.3.5a: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).
standards.L.3.5b: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).
standards.L.3.5c: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty.
standards.L.3.6: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic and domain-specific words, including words signaling spatial and temporal relationships.

units.title: Fables and Folktales: Lessons in Stories
units.big_idea: Stories from around the world teach lessons through characters' choices.

units.title: Novel Study: Charlotte's Web
units.big_idea: Characters change through friendship, and authors use details to show who characters are.

units.title: Animal Adaptations: Reading and Writing to Inform
units.big_idea: Informational texts are organized to help readers learn; writers organize facts to teach others.

units.title: Myths of Ancient Greece
units.big_idea: Myths explained the world and taught values; their lessons still matter today.

units.title: Poetry: Sound, Image and Feeling
units.big_idea: Poets choose words, line breaks and sound patterns to create images and feelings.

units.title: Biographies of Courage and Opinion Writing
units.big_idea: Real people show courage, and writers support opinions with reasons from texts.

units.title: Novel Study: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
units.big_idea: Journeys reveal what characters already have inside them.

units.title: Research: California's Natural Wonders
units.big_idea: Researchers gather, sort and share information from multiple sources.

units.title: Author Study and Readers' Theater
units.big_idea: Authors return to favorite characters, and performing stories brings them to life.

objectives: Establish a daily independent reading routine
Recount fables and state the moral

days.title: Reading launch
days.work: Choose a library book for a 20-minute independent reading routine and start a reading log; read 'The Lion and the Mouse' and discuss its moral.

days.title: Recount a fable
days.work: Read 'The Tortoise and the Hare,' retell it in 5 sentences using first/next/then/finally, and spell closed vs. open syllable words (rab-bit, ti-ger).

days.title: Sentence types
days.work: Learn the four sentence types and end punctuation; find each type in 'The Fox and the Crow' and write one of each about the fable.

days.title: Writing a memory
days.work: Brainstorm small-moment memories and draft a half-page narrative about a time you learned a lesson.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a spelling check on syllable types, answer 4 text-based questions on a new fable, and discuss its lesson aloud using complete sentences.

weeks.assessment: Fable comprehension questions, spelling check, narrative draft

objectives: Describe characters' traits and how actions lead to a lesson

days.title: Character traits
days.work: Read 'The Ant and the Grasshopper' and fill a trait chart for each character with text evidence.

days.title: Vowel teams
days.work: Sort and spell ai/ay and ee/ea words, then read 'The Boy Who Cried Wolf' aloud for fluency.

days.title: Nouns
days.work: Identify common and proper nouns in 'The Boy Who Cried Wolf' and write 5 sentences using both.

days.title: Narrative leads
days.work: Revise the first paragraph of your personal narrative with a strong lead (action, dialogue or sound).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining how one character's actions taught the moral, then partner-discuss which fable lesson matters most.

weeks.assessment: Character paragraph with evidence; noun practice sheet

objectives: Compare lessons in folktales from different cultures

days.title: Anansi tales
days.work: Read an Anansi the Spider folktale and identify the trickster's problem, choices and lesson.

days.title: Stone Soup
days.work: Read a version of 'Stone Soup' and chart how the villagers change from start to end; spell r-controlled words (ar, or, er, ir, ur).

days.title: Plural nouns
days.work: Practice regular (-s, -es) and irregular plurals (mouse/mice, child/children) with a sorting activity and sentences.

days.title: Revise for detail
days.work: Add sensory details and feelings to the middle of your personal narrative, using a revision checklist.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Compare the lessons of Anansi and Stone Soup in a Venn diagram and discuss with a family member.

weeks.assessment: Venn diagram comparison; plural nouns check

days.title: Abstract nouns
days.work: Learn abstract nouns (kindness, courage, friendship) and identify the abstract noun each fable teaches about.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Edit your narrative for capitals, end punctuation and plurals; practice prefixes un- and re- in spelling.

days.title: Ending
days.work: Write a satisfying ending that reflects on the lesson learned, then publish a final copy.

days.title: Fluency
days.work: Practice reading a fable aloud 3 times for expression and record yourself.

days.title: Unit 1 assessment
days.work: Read a new fable and answer questions on moral and character, take the un-/re- spelling test, and read your narrative aloud.

weeks.assessment: Unit 1 reading assessment; published narrative scored with rubric

objectives: Ask and answer questions with text evidence

days.title: Chapters 1–2
days.work: Read chapters 1–2 and describe Fern's character with evidence; discuss whether Fern's father was fair.

days.title: Chapter 3–4
days.work: Read chapters 3–4 and write 3 questions and answers about Wilbur's loneliness; spell dis- and pre- words.

days.title: Verbs
days.work: Identify action and linking verbs in a passage from chapter 4 and write 6 sentences about the barn.

days.title: Chapter 5
days.work: Read chapter 5 and describe first impressions of Charlotte using a character web.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a chapters 1–5 quiz and a prefix spelling check (dis-, pre-, mis-).

objectives: Explain how characters' actions move the plot

days.title: Chapters 6–7
days.work: Read chapters 6–7 and explain how Wilbur learns his fate and how it changes the plot.

days.title: Verb tenses
days.work: Write sentences about the novel in past, present and future tense; spell -ful and -less words.

days.title: Chapters 8–9
days.work: Read chapters 8–9 and explain how each chapter builds on the last in a plot chart.

days.title: Story plan
days.work: Plan an original animal story with a story map (characters, setting, problem, events, solution).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on how Charlotte's plan begins and take a verb tense quiz.

objectives: Determine meanings of words and phrases

days.title: Chapters 11–12
days.work: Read chapters 11–12 and discuss why the web words ('Some Pig') work; list strong words Charlotte chooses.

days.title: Irregular verbs
days.work: Practice irregular past tense verbs (spin/spun, write/wrote, catch/caught) using sentences about the book; spell -ly and -ness words.

days.title: Chapters 13–14
days.work: Read chapters 13–14 and figure out the meaning of 5 tricky words from context.

days.title: Draft story
days.work: Draft the beginning and middle of your animal story with at least 2 lines of dialogue.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an irregular verbs quiz and answer comprehension questions on chapters 11–15.

days.title: Chapters 16–17
days.work: Read chapters 16–17 (the fair) and describe Templeton's motivation.

days.title: Dialogue punctuation
days.work: Copy dialogue from the novel and learn quotation mark and comma rules; spell words with -ed and -ing using the doubling rule.

days.title: Chapters 18–19
days.work: Read chapters 18–19 and chart how Wilbur has changed since chapter 1.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise your story's dialogue for correct punctuation and temporal words (later, meanwhile).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a dialogue punctuation check and discuss Charlotte's sacrifice in a family book talk.

weeks.assessment: Dialogue punctuation check; book talk participation

weeks.topic: Charlotte's Web, chapters 20–22 and story publishing
objectives: Determine the theme of the novel

days.title: Chapters 20–22
days.work: Finish the novel and discuss the theme of friendship and the cycle of life.

days.title: Theme
days.work: Write a paragraph stating the novel's theme supported by 2 quotations; spell drop-e words (hope/hoping).

days.title: Publish
days.work: Edit and publish your animal story with illustrations.

days.title: Book talk
days.work: Give a 2-minute book talk recommending Charlotte's Web to a friend.

days.title: Unit 2 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 2 test (comprehension, vocabulary, verbs, dialogue) and share your published story.

objectives: Use text features to locate information

days.title: Text feature hunt
days.work: Find headings, captions, bold words, glossary and index in an animal nonfiction book and explain each feature's job.

days.title: Main idea
days.work: Read a ReadWorks passage on camouflage and identify the main idea and 3 supporting details.

days.title: Adjectives
days.work: Identify adjectives in animal descriptions and write 5 descriptive sentences; spell change-y-to-i words (cry/cries).

days.title: Choose an animal
days.work: Select an animal for an informational report and write 5 questions you want to answer.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer text-feature questions on a new passage and take the spelling check.

weeks.assessment: Text feature check; main idea organizer

objectives: Describe cause/effect relationships in scientific texts
Compare a pourquoi tale to fact
materials: Just So Stories by Rudyard Kipling (Project Gutenberg)

days.title: Just So Story
days.work: Read Kipling's 'How the Leopard Got His Spots' and discuss how a pourquoi tale explains nature.

days.title: Real reasons
days.work: Read a nonfiction passage on leopard camouflage and complete a cause/effect chart.

days.title: Comparatives
days.work: Use comparative and superlative adjectives (faster, fastest) to compare animal features; spell -able and -ible words.

days.title: Note taking
days.work: Take notes on your report animal from 2 sources, sorting facts into body, habitat, food and adaptations.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph comparing the fiction and nonfiction explanations of the leopard's spots.

weeks.assessment: Fiction vs. nonfiction paragraph; notes check

days.title: Report plan
days.work: Organize notes into an outline with an introduction, 3 topic paragraphs and conclusion.

days.title: Diagrams
days.work: Study a labeled diagram of an animal and explain what it adds to the words; spell -tion and -sion words.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft introduction and first two paragraphs using linking words (also, another, and, but).

days.title: Commas
days.work: Practice commas in a series and in addresses by writing a letter to a zoo asking a question.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Finish the report draft and read it to a family member for feedback on clarity.

weeks.assessment: Report draft; letter with correct comma use

objectives: Revise and publish an informational report with a text feature

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise the report for definitions of key words and a strong conclusion; spell -ment and -er/-or words.

days.title: Add text features
days.work: Add a heading, labeled diagram, caption and glossary to the published report.

days.title: Video listening
days.work: Watch a short nature video on your animal and note main ideas and details.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present your report to the family and answer 3 questions.

days.title: Unit 3 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 3 test on main idea, text features and cause/effect with a new passage.

objectives: Recount a myth and determine its lesson
materials: A Wonder-Book for Girls and Boys by Nathaniel Hawthorne (Project Gutenberg)

days.title: What is a myth?
days.work: Learn about Ancient Greece and the Olympian gods, then make a gods chart with symbols.

days.title: Pandora
days.work: Read the Pandora myth ('The Paradise of Children') and recount it in sequence.

days.title: Agreement
days.work: Practice subject-verb agreement with sentences about the gods; study Greek roots (bio, graph, photo).

days.title: Lesson
days.work: Write what lesson the Pandora myth teaches about curiosity.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a subject-verb agreement quiz and answer questions on the Pandora myth.

objectives: Begin opinion writing about a text

days.title: King Midas
days.work: Read 'The Golden Touch' and chart Midas's wishes, actions and consequences.

days.title: Arachne
days.work: Read the myth of Arachne and Athena and describe Arachne's pride with evidence.

days.title: Pronouns
days.work: Practice pronoun-antecedent agreement in sentences about both myths; spell diphthongs oi/oy, ou/ow.

days.title: Opinion plan
days.work: Plan an opinion paragraph: Which character learned the hardest lesson? Give 2 reasons.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write the opinion paragraph with linking words and discuss it in a book talk.

days.title: Persephone
days.work: Read the Persephone myth and explain how it explained the seasons.

days.title: Illustrations
days.work: Compare two illustrations of Icarus and explain how each shows mood.

days.title: Icarus
days.work: Read the Icarus myth and discuss nonliteral phrases like 'flying too close to the sun.'

days.title: Capitalize titles
days.work: Write the titles of all myths and books read so far with correct capitalization; spell homophones (their/there/they're).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer questions about both myths and listen to a family member's retelling, asking 3 questions.

days.title: Myth plan
days.work: Plan an original myth explaining a natural event (why the moon changes shape) with a story map.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft the myth using a god or hero character and dialogue; spell irregular words (said, laugh, though).

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise the myth for a clear lesson and strong verbs.

days.title: Present
days.work: Read the myth aloud with expression to an audience.

days.title: Unit 4 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 4 test on myths, agreement and capitalization.

objectives: Use poetry terms to describe parts of poems
materials: A Child's Garden of Verses by Robert Louis Stevenson (Project Gutenberg)

days.title: Stanzas
days.work: Read Stevenson's 'My Shadow' and label lines and stanzas; describe what each stanza adds.

days.title: Rhythm
days.work: Clap the rhythm of 'The Swing' and practice reading it aloud with expression; spell VCCV multisyllable words.

days.title: Literal vs. nonliteral
days.work: Find nonliteral phrases in poems and draw literal vs. real meanings.

days.title: Write a poem
days.work: Write a rhyming poem in 2 stanzas about a shadow or swing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Record a fluent reading of a Stevenson poem and complete a poetry terms check.

objectives: Explain how word choice creates images
materials: 'Who Has Seen the Wind?' by Christina Rossetti
'April Rain Song' by Langston Hughes (library anthology)

days.title: Rossetti
days.work: Read 'Who Has Seen the Wind?' and sketch the images the poet creates.

days.title: Hughes
days.work: Read 'April Rain Song' and list sensory words; spell VCV words (cab-in, ti-ger).

days.title: Shades of meaning
days.work: Order related words on a line (whisper, say, shout; think, believe, know).

days.title: Free verse
days.work: Write a free-verse poem about weather using sensory words.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain in writing how one poet's word choice creates a feeling.

weeks.assessment: Word choice response; shades of meaning check

objectives: Create an audio recording of poems

days.title: Word connections
days.work: Describe people and places in your life with words from the poems (cozy, gentle, noisy).

days.title: Poem types
days.work: Read and write an acrostic and a cinquain; spell consonant-le words (table, puzzle).

days.title: Anthology
days.work: Compile 6 favorite poems (3 published, 3 original) into an illustrated anthology.

days.title: Record
days.work: Record a poetry podcast reading 3 poems fluently.

days.title: Unit 5 assessment
days.work: Complete a poetry test on terms, nonliteral language and imagery.

weeks.assessment: Unit 5 test; poetry anthology and recording

objectives: Describe a sequence of events in a person's life
materials: The Story of My Life by Helen Keller (Project Gutenberg, chapter 4 excerpt)

days.title: Biography basics
days.work: Compare biography and autobiography; start a timeline of Helen Keller's life.

days.title: Primary account
days.work: Read the water-pump excerpt from 'The Story of My Life' and discuss how she felt.

days.title: Conjunctions
days.work: Combine sentences about Helen Keller using and, but, or, so; spell over-, under-, sub- words.

days.title: Main idea
days.work: Identify the main idea of a biography chapter and its key details.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete the timeline and write a summary of Helen Keller's achievements.

weeks.topic: Biography: Ruby Bridges and Jackie Robinson
objectives: Distinguish own point of view from the author's
materials: The Story of Ruby Bridges by Robert Coles (library)

days.title: Ruby Bridges
days.work: Read 'The Story of Ruby Bridges' and discuss the courage she showed.

days.title: Jackie Robinson
days.work: Read a Jackie Robinson biography and list challenges he faced.

days.title: Subordinating conjunctions
days.work: Write complex sentences with because, when, although, after; study Latin roots port and rupt.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare the two people's challenges and actions in a chart; write how your view differs from the author's.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Hold a discussion on 'What is courage?' using evidence from both texts.

objectives: Write an opinion essay with reasons from texts
Write simple, compound and complex sentences

days.title: Opinion choice
days.work: Choose which person showed the greatest courage and list reasons with evidence.

days.title: Organizer
days.work: Plan an essay with introduction, 3 reasons with evidence and conclusion; study roots struct and tract.

days.title: Sentence variety
days.work: Practice simple, compound and complex sentences about your person.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft the essay with linking words (because, therefore, for example).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read the draft to a partner and get 2 compliments and 1 suggestion.

objectives: Revise and type an opinion essay

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise reasons and conclusion using the opinion rubric.

days.title: Type it
days.work: Type the final essay, practicing keyboarding; study Greek roots tele, phon, scope.

days.title: Speech
days.work: Turn the essay into a 2-minute speech with note cards.

days.title: Deliver
days.work: Deliver the speech to family, speaking clearly and making eye contact.

days.title: Unit 6 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 6 test on biographies, conjunctions and sentence types.

weeks.assessment: Unit 6 test; published opinion essay rubric

weeks.topic: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, chapters 1–6
objectives: Distinguish own point of view from characters'
materials: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (Project Gutenberg)

days.title: Chapters 1–2
days.work: Read chapters 1–2 and contrast Kansas and Oz with descriptive details.

days.title: Chapters 3–4
days.work: Read chapters 3–4 and describe the Scarecrow; spell silent-letter words (kn, wr, gh).

days.title: Adverbs
days.work: Use comparative and superlative adverbs (faster, most carefully) in sentences about the journey.

days.title: Chapters 5–6
days.work: Read chapters 5–6 and write whether you agree with the Tin Woodman's view that a heart matters most.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a chapters 1–6 quiz and a point-of-view journal entry.

weeks.topic: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, chapters 7–12
objectives: Explain how illustrations contribute to the story
materials: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz with W.W. Denslow illustrations

days.title: Chapters 7–9
days.work: Read chapters 7–9 and describe the Cowardly Lion's brave actions.

days.title: Illustrations
days.work: Study 3 Denslow illustrations and explain what they show about mood and character.

days.title: Possessives
days.work: Write singular and plural possessives (Dorothy's shoes, the witches' castle); spell soft c and g words.

days.title: Chapters 10–12
days.work: Read chapters 10–12 and chart each character's wish and the Wizard's demand.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a possessives quiz and write a character trait paragraph.

weeks.topic: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, chapters 13–18

days.title: Chapters 13–15
days.work: Read chapters 13–15 and discuss why the Wizard is a 'humbug.'

days.title: Chapters 16–18
days.work: Read chapters 16–18 and explain how the Wizard 'gives' each friend a gift.

days.title: Word choice
days.work: Replace weak words with vivid ones in a passage and explain the effect; spell schwa words (-al, -el).

days.title: Theme
days.work: Write a paragraph about the theme 'you already have what you need' with evidence.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Hold a book discussion and answer comprehension questions on chapters 13–18.

weeks.topic: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, chapters 19–24

days.title: Chapters 19–21
days.work: Read chapters 19–21 and track the journey south on a map of Oz.

days.title: Chapters 22–24
days.work: Finish the novel and recount the main events in a summary.

days.title: Spoken vs. written
days.work: Rewrite informal spoken lines into formal written English and vice versa; spell contractions.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Plan a new Oz adventure for Dorothy with a new character and setting.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete an end-of-novel quiz.

weeks.topic: Oz narrative and book vs. film
objectives: Write a narrative with dialogue and descriptive details

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft the new Oz adventure with dialogue and temporal words.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise for word choice and correct dialogue punctuation; spell -ous and -ive words.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare a scene from the book to a film version and discuss differences.

days.title: Publish
days.work: Publish the narrative with an illustration.

days.title: Unit 7 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 7 test and share your Oz story aloud.

objectives: Use search tools and text features

days.title: Choose a topic
days.work: Choose a California natural wonder (Yosemite, redwoods, Death Valley, Monterey Bay) and write 5 research questions.

days.title: Search tools
days.work: Use keyword searches and an index to find sources; record titles in a source list.

days.title: Dictionary
days.work: Use a dictionary and glossary to define 6 domain words; spell inter- and trans- words.

days.title: Read sources
days.work: Read 2 sources and highlight answers to your questions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Turn in question list and source list for review.

objectives: Take notes and sort evidence into categories
Compare two texts on the same topic

days.title: Note cards
days.work: Take notes in your own words on note cards from source 1.

days.title: Sort notes
days.work: Sort note cards into categories (location, plants and animals, history, visiting).

days.title: Compare sources
days.work: Compare key points from two sources on your topic in a chart.

days.title: Context clues
days.work: Use context clues to figure out unknown words in your sources; review affixes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on what two sources agree and disagree on.

objectives: Write an informative report from notes

days.title: Outline
days.work: Organize notes into a report outline.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft introduction and two body paragraphs.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Finish the body and conclusion; add a map with caption.

days.title: Affixes
days.work: Determine meanings of words formed with affixes in the report (unprotected, rebuild); review homographs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Self-check the draft against the research rubric.

days.title: Revise and edit
days.work: Revise and edit the report with an adult.

days.title: Publish
days.work: Type and publish the report with a photo and map.

days.title: Visual display
days.work: Create a slideshow or poster for the presentation.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present research to the family and answer questions.

days.title: Unit 8 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 8 test on informational reading and research skills.

weeks.assessment: Unit 8 test; research report and presentation rubric

objectives: Compare themes, settings and plots of stories by the same author with the same characters
materials: The Tale of Peter Rabbit and The Tale of Benjamin Bunny by Beatrix Potter (Project Gutenberg)

days.title: Peter Rabbit
days.work: Read 'The Tale of Peter Rabbit' and map its plot.

days.title: Benjamin Bunny
days.work: Read 'The Tale of Benjamin Bunny' and map its plot.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare settings, plots and themes of the two tales in a chart; review dictionary syllable guides.

days.title: Response
days.work: Write a comparison paragraph about the two tales.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer comparison questions and read a Potter passage aloud fluently.

objectives: Refer to parts of a drama using scene terms
materials: readers' theater script adapted from a fable or Potter tale

days.title: Script features
days.work: Read a readers' theater script and identify cast list, scenes and stage directions.

days.title: Write a script
days.work: Convert a fable into a short script, turning narrative into dialogue.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse the script with expression and timing.

days.title: Perform
days.work: Perform for family and record it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Reflect on the performance and identify how scenes build on each other.

objectives: Reflect on growth as a reader and writer

days.title: Reading review
days.work: Review the reading log and choose top 3 books; write a recommendation.

days.title: Writing portfolio
days.work: Select the best narrative, informative and opinion pieces for a portfolio.

days.title: Final assessment
days.work: Complete the end-of-year reading, spelling and grammar assessment.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write a letter to your future 4th-grade self about your growth.

days.title: Celebrate
days.work: Share your portfolio at a family reading celebration and set a summer reading goal.
